name: M1 Procar
hook: When the racing it was built for fell through, BMW invented a championship of its own and put Formula One drivers in it.
story: Picture BMW in the late 1970s. It wants a racing supercar. So it asks Lamborghini to help build one, the M1. Then Lamborghini runs out of money. BMW has to pull the project back and finish it elsewhere. By the time the M1 is ready, the sports car racing it was made for has moved on. The car is late, and very expensive. Road sales are slow. So BMW does something bold. It invents a series of its own, called Procar. Every car is an M1. They race on Saturdays, on the same weekend as Formula One. And the fastest Formula One drivers from practice get works cars. So you could watch Niki Lauda, Nelson Piquet and Alan Jones bang doors in identical BMWs. Lauda wins in 1979. Piquet wins in 1980. Then BMW ends it to focus on Formula One itself. Two seasons, and that was all. Today a Procar is one of the most loved racing BMWs ever made.
description: The M1 Procar was the racing version of the BMW M1, BMW's first mid-engined car, developed with early help from Lamborghini and designed by Giorgetto Giugiaro. It used a 3.5-litre straight-six making about 470 hp, fibreglass bodywork over a steel frame, and weighed 1,020 kg. When its intended racing class fell through, BMW created the one-make Procar Championship for 1979 and 1980, run at Formula One weekends. Niki Lauda and Nelson Piquet were its two champions.
